headline: A WWII Veteran at 100 Still Carves Wooden Toys for Children Worldwide
meta_description: Despite losing his eyesight, a centenarian WWII veteran continues handcrafting wooden cars for children overseas, having made over 1,000 in a decade.
summary_short: At 100 years old and losing his sight, a WWII veteran hasn't slowed down—he's made over 1,000 handmade wooden cars for children he'll never meet.
body:
At 100 years old and losing his eyesight, a WWII veteran continues handcrafting wooden cars for children overseas he will never meet.

Over the past decade, he has produced more than 1,000 of these toys, driven by a quiet commitment to bring joy to young lives across borders. This year alone, he has completed more than 100 vehicles for Operation, demonstrating that neither age nor fading vision diminishes his determination to give.

His steady hands and unwavering resolve stand as a testament to a life shaped by service. Each wooden car represents not just craftsmanship, but a tangible connection between a man marking a century of life and children who will hold his work in their hands—a legacy measured not in recognition, but in the simple happiness of a gift made with care.
quick_facts: WWII veteran, now 100 years old, handcrafts wooden cars
Made over 1,000 toys in the past decade
Completed more than 100 cars this year for Operation
